title: Sennacherib's siege of Jerusalem
description: Added from the Generations curriculum import (Preparing the World for Jesus (1st ed., 2020)). Kevin ruled (2026-10-27) that Jones's first invasion, as Tartan (713 BC), is this event. That Appendix F row sets the sort. Jones's second invasion (709 BC) is a separate record.

sorting_basis.note: Tier 3: Ussher-Jones (Floyd Nolen Jones): 713 BC (no higher-tier year available).

chronologies.note: pending CFAH reference (the CFAH series does not cover this period; no tier 1–4 date exists)

chronologies.citation: Jones, The Chronology of the Old Testament: A Return to the Basics, 23rd ed. (Master Books, 2026), Appendix F, printed p. 279 (PDF p. 314)
chronologies.note: Kevin ruled (2026-10-27) that Jones's first invasion, as Tartan (713 BC), is this event. The record sennacherib-first-invasion was merged here. Jones's second invasion (709 BC, as pro-rex) is sennacherib-second-invasion and does not set this year.

chronologies.citation: Preparing the World for Jesus (1st ed., 2020), ch. 10 "The Assyrian Empire: Power by Cruelty (1200–612 BC)", PDF p. 324 (printed p. 323)
chronologies.note: Timeline Review: "Sennacherib's Siege on Jerusalem". Sennacherib ruled 705-681 BC (p. 307).

chronologies.note: From the book's "Ancient Empires" pages (credited in an image to Daily Bible Study, keyway.ca). Reign of Sennacherib.

chronologies.date: “when Sanacharib, king of the Arabians and Assyrians, marched his vast army into Egypt”
chronologies.citation: Herodotus, Histories 2.141 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 157 (PDF p. 159)
chronologies.note: Sethos, priest of Vulcan, meets Sanacharib at Pelusium; field-mice gnaw the Assyrian bowstrings. Linked to Sennacherib's campaign of 2 Kings 18–19 (the record's Scripture); the identification is traditional, not stated by Herodotus.
